entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Counsel for Opposite Party :- A.G.A.
Hon'ble Sudhir Agarwal,J.
1.

Heard Sri Narendra Pratap Singh, learned counsel for revisionist and learned AGA for State of U.P.
2.

This criminal revision under Section 397/401 Cr.P.C., has been filed aggrieved by judgement and order dated 26.10.1988 passed by Sri Hari Shankar Sharma, Special/ Additional Sessions Judge,
Mathura in Criminal Appeal No. 132 of 1988 dismissing the same and upholding judgement and order dated 26.10.1988 passed by Sri Magan Lal, Judicial Magistrate, Arthik Apradh, Mathura (J.M.E.O) in Criminal Case No. 323 of 1986 convicting applicant under Section 7/16 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and sentenced him to undergo six months rigorous imprisonment and also to pay a fine of Rs. 1000/- and in default of payment of fine, to undergo further six months rigorous imprisonment.

Devi Singh vs State Of U.P. on 17 July, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91766212/
1 3.

entities.text: Devi Singh vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: At the very outset, learned counsel for revisionist, states that he is not assailing judgment of Courts below on merits, but is seeking mercy stating that this is an old matter and is now attained advance age, therefore, sentence of imprisonment awarded to him be reduced.

4. Looking to the entire facts and circumstances, I find that Court below had awarded minimum sentence to revisionist of six months rigorous imprisonment with aforesaid fine which has been confirmed by Appellate Court.
Since minimum sentence has been awarded by Courts below which is prescribed in Statute and where the minimum sentence prescribed, Court cannot reduce the same.
Certify this judgment to the lower Court immediately.

Order Date :- 17.7.2019 Siddhant Sahu  Devi Singh vs State Of U.P. on 17 July, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91766212/
